blocks.text: The census shows an estate of 174.3 TiB. The object store holds 130.3 TiB, which is 74.8% of the estate. File shares hold 43.6 TiB, which is 25.0%. Databases hold 0.3 TiB, which is 0.2%. Storage decisions therefore sit mainly in the object store and the file shares, not in the databases.

On cost, 41.9 TiB of the object store has not been written for over a year, and 7.7 TiB are duplicate candidates. Priced strategies bound the monthly saving at 1,174.4 USD at reference list prices. That is an upper bound, not the owner's invoice or a realised saving. 40 of 106 buckets could not be read.

On condition and products, 23.0% of database rows are degraded, 81.7% carry empty required-looking fields and 71.8% of sampled rows carry personal-data markers. These are preparation tasks. The owner has declared rights established, so no recommendation depends on rights. Three products are proposed as first specifications.

terms.meaning: Space that could be removed or stored more cheaply once the check named beside it has been done. It is not space already freed, and it is not a guaranteed saving — the monthly figures are upper bounds at list prices.
Nothing new has been written to that bucket or table for more than a year, judged by the newest write date we could see. It says nothing about whether anyone still reads it — that was not measured.
terms.term: Cold (not written for over a year)

terms.meaning: Two objects whose size and storage fingerprint (ETag) match inside the same store. For large uploads that fingerprint is not a content hash, so a candidate must be confirmed by hashing before any copy is removed.
Database rows that are identical in every measured column. 'Normalised' duplicates also match after trimming spaces and case.
A row whose worst column shows damage: text cut short, a placeholder such as 'N/A' or 'test', an invalid format, stray whitespace or garbled characters.

Blank values in columns whose name or pattern suggests they should always be filled (for example an identifier or a date). The database may not formally require them; the census flags them so an owner can decide.
A column that is empty on practically every row: schema carried without data.
A sampled value that looks like an email, phone number, national ID or similar. It is a condition of the data, not a judgement about rights — the owner has declared all rights established.
A cheaper storage tier for data that is kept but rarely opened. Retrieval is slower and carries its own fee, which is why the saving is stated as an upper bound.
Where this pack suggests data should live or how it should be tiered. Every destination here is a proposal for the executive to approve; this pack moved and deleted nothing.
Recorded hours multiplied by the share of two-second windows the admitted music detector did not call music. Silence is set aside first.
The share of labelled windows (or transcript passages) where the model's language label matched the folder the recording was filed under. It is a model reading, not a human verification.
Windows where the language model's confidence fell below its threshold, so it gave no language rather than guess.

A calendar date on which a station has at least one news script in the archive, and the distinct hour slots scripted that day. The archive does not carry a script for every hour of every day; the tables show exactly which days and hours it does.
The retained Akki record (census run, GPU job or database reading) that every figure in this pack is traced to. The appendix lists them; the workbook carries the row-level evidence.

blocks.text: Of 8 candidates, the proposed first specifications are reference and master data, the content catalogue and channel engagement analytics. Each is graded C, and most supporting tables carry personal-data markers. This is a recommendation, not a measured commercial ranking.

First tasks differ. Reference data needs canonical fields and completeness checks. The catalogue needs reconciliation and identifier removal. Channel analytics needs aggregation by channel and time, and metric validation. Each needs a buyer-side review of fit, and no revenue or semantic fit is claimed.

The decisions table sets out ten decisions, each with its source, action, proposed destination or rule, responsible role and benefit. Money is stated as an upper bound. The anchors are 41.9 TiB of write-inactive bytes, 7.7 TiB of duplicate candidates, 40 unreadable buckets and 1,174.4 USD a month at list prices.
The owner is asked to approve named validation and preparation work with accountable roles and acceptance checks. Destinations remain provisional and nothing has been executed.

blocks.text: Only 638 of 1006 tables were measured, so sampled ratios need a complete-pass census. 40 buckets need reconciling with the provider, and 43.6 TiB of file shares in 1.5m files need fingerprinting.

3540 transcripts remain unread, script language is unassessed, and overlap between workbench and staged recordings needs a hash join. These are measurement gaps with defined closing tasks, not adverse findings.

First, test archive tiering on the 41.9 TiB of write-inactive object bytes, checking read patterns and retrieval fees against the 1,174.4 USD monthly upper bound. Second, confirm the 7.7 TiB of duplicate candidates by content hash. Third, reconcile the 40 unreadable buckets and fingerprint the file shares.

Then prepare one bounded product from the shortlist, with a buyer-side review. Keep database cleanup of about 15.2 GiB, which is 4.3% of bytes, as a separate narrower workstream. The order follows size and certainty: the largest bytes need the cheapest checks first.

sections.heading: What to do first, in order

blocks.text: Coverage is the main limit. Database measures cover 638 of 1006 tables. The 71.8% personal-data marker share comes from sampled rows, and one connection could not be read. Unreadable buckets and unfingerprinted shares leave duplication open, and 7.7 TiB is candidates only.
The 1,174.4 USD monthly figure is a list-price upper bound, not the owner's bill. Audio and transcript readings are model readings. Settled rights are separate from these operational checks.
